::: {.sos-disclaimer}
**Preliminary analysis using publicly available data.** Trade flows from BACI; complexity from the Harvard Growth Lab; de-risking from IMF bilateral FDI; FATF greylist and EU AMLD timing from public sources. See the [Methodology](method.qmd) and [Data](data.qmd) pages for limitations.
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
import {choropleth, quadrantScatter} from "./_ojs/charts.js";
import {countryHref} from "./_ojs/router.js";
import {fmt2} from "./_ojs/format.js";
Plot = require("@observablehq/plot@0.6")
d3   = require("d3@7")
htl  = require("htl@0.3")
topojson = require("topojson-client@3")
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
sos = await FileAttachment("_data/sos_country.json").json()
sosByIso3 = new Map(sos.map(d => [d.iso3, d]))
worldWithIso3 = await FileAttachment("_data/world.geojson").json()
```

## Composite SOS across the world

::: {.sos-caption}
Higher values flag countries where complex-goods trade is most exposed to correspondent-banking frictions. Hover for country, score, and rank.
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
choropleth(Plot, worldWithIso3, sosByIso3, {height: 480})
```

## Top 20 by composite SOS

::: {.sos-caption}
Click a country in the table or use the selector below to open its country page.
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
top20 = sos
  .filter(d => d.sos_composite != null && d.rank_composite != null)
  .sort((a, b) => a.rank_composite - b.rank_composite)
  .slice(0, 20)
  .map(d => ({
    Rank: d.rank_composite,
    Country: d.name,
    ISO3: d.iso3,
    "Composite SOS": +d.sos_composite,
    FATF:  d.sos_fatf  != null ? +d.sos_fatf  : null,
    FDI:   d.sos_fdi   != null ? +d.sos_fdi   : null,
    AMLD:  d.sos_amld  != null ? +d.sos_amld  : null,
    "Quadrant": d.quadrant_label || ""
  }))

Inputs.table(top20, {
  format: {
    "Composite SOS": x => x == null ? "—" : x.toFixed(2),
    "FATF":  x => x == null ? "—" : x.toFixed(2),
    "FDI":   x => x == null ? "—" : x.toFixed(2),
    "AMLD":  x => x == null ? "—" : x.toFixed(2),
    "Rank":  x => x == null ? "—" : Math.round(x)
  },
  align: {Rank: "right", "Composite SOS": "right", FATF: "right", FDI: "right", AMLD: "right"},
  rows: 20
})
```

## Open a country

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof picked = Inputs.select(
  sos.slice().sort((a, b) => (a.name || "").localeCompare(b.name || "")),
  {label: "Country", format: x => `${x.name} (${x.iso3})`, value: sos.find(d => d.iso3 === "HTI") || sos[0]}
)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  if (!picked || !picked.iso3) return htl.html`<div class="sos-caption">Pick a country to open its profile.</div>`;
  const url = countryHref(picked.iso3);
  return htl.html`<div class="sos-caption">
    Open <a href="${url}"><strong>${picked.name}</strong> (${picked.iso3})</a>
    or pick another country above.
  </div>`;
}
```

## Feasibility quadrant

::: {.sos-caption}
Capital openness (Chinn-Ito) on x; infrastructure / GDP-per-capita score on y; bubble size and color = composite SOS. Q1 (top-right) flags actionable-now jurisdictions; Q4 (bottom-left) is structurally blocked.
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
quadrantScatter(Plot, sos, {height: 460})
```

## How to read this

- **Composite SOS** rolls up three independent natural experiments — FATF greylisting, FDI-derisked corridors, and EU AMLD harmonization — into a single country-level score. Higher = more exposure to correspondent-banking frictions on complex-goods trade.
- **Three components** (FATF / FDI / AMLD) decompose the headline score and identify which channel dominates for each country.
- **Quadrants** combine the SOS with two readiness dimensions (capital openness × infrastructure) so an analyst can separate _high-need_ from _actionable-now_ jurisdictions.
